model_annotation: The bar chart illustrates the effects of various mBERT and XLM models on different language families and isolated languages, with error bars indicating variability. The horizontal axis categorizes the data by language family (IE-Baltic, IE-Germanic, IE-Indic, IE-Romance, IE-Slavic, IE-other, Isolate, Semitic, Uralic) and the vertical axis measures the effect on a numerical scale from 0 to 30. Each category on the x-axis displays a group of bars representing different models: mBERT-L₂ (light blue), XLM-L₂ (dark blue), mBERT-R₂ (light green), XLM-R₂ (dark green), mBERT-B₂ (light red), and XLM-B₂ (dark red). The legend clarifies the color coding for each model. The chart shows that the IE-Indic family has the highest effect values, with mBERT-L₂, XLM-L₂, mBERT-R₂, XLM-R₂, mBERT-B₂, and XLM-B₂ all exceeding 20. In contrast, the Isolate and Uralic categories show much lower effects, with most models having values close to zero. The error bars, representing standard deviation or confidence intervals, vary in length across categories and models, indicating differing levels of uncertainty in the measurements.
